The constraint we start with

What slows hospitality teams down.

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

01

Inquiries arrive everywhere, at all hours

Guests write on WhatsApp, Instagram, Google, OTA inboxes and email, or call late at night. When replies wait for the morning shift, the guest books the next property, table or tour they find, often through a channel that charges commission.

02

Distribution leaks margin

OTA and food aggregator commissions are part of the business, but rate inconsistencies, stale menus and missed direct inquiries deepen that dependence. Few teams have the time to check every channel, every day.

03

Front-desk compliance is manual and time-bound

Hotels record guest identity details and, for foreign nationals, send Form III particulars through the Bureau of Immigration portal within twenty-four hours of arrival and of departure. Paper registers and retyping at a busy desk create queues and late filings.

04

Requests and complaints fall between teams

A towel request, a broken AC, a late tour pickup or a missing decorator moves by phone, radio and personal WhatsApp. Nobody sees what is open, who owns it or how long the guest has waited until the complaint reaches a review site.

05

Reviews shape demand, but replies lag

Google, OTA and aggregator ratings drive discovery. Managers know they should reply thoughtfully and act on private feedback, but the volume across platforms, properties and outlets makes that slip.

06

Thin food margins hide in daily data

Restaurants and cloud kitchens juggle POS sales, aggregator payouts, several brands from one kitchen and stock that spoils. Without a reliable daily close, wastage and settlement gaps surface weeks later, if at all.

The perfect automation

Booking-to-checkout guest concierge on WhatsApp

One connected flow from the moment a room is booked to the review after checkout. Guests get timely WhatsApp updates and a secure pre-check-in link. The front desk gets verified particulars and a Form III deadline tracker. In-stay requests reach the right team with a clock running, and every stay ends with feedback, recovery and a manager-approved review reply.

  1. 01

    Sync bookings and consent

    Reservations from the PMS, channel manager and booking engine flow into one guest record with stay dates, room type, source and any messaging consent. OTA bookings usually arrive without WhatsApp opt-in, so those guests get the first message by email or DLT-registered SMS and can opt in on the form.

    nn8nSSupabaseRResend
  2. 02

    Pre-arrival message and secure pre-check-in

    An approved WhatsApp utility template shares check-in time, directions and a link to a pre-check-in form on the hotel's own domain. Guests confirm arrival time and ID details there, never in the chat, and can choose priced extras such as an airport transfer or early check-in.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformNNext.jsSSupabase
  3. 03

    Verify at arrival and track Form III

    The front desk sees each arrival's pre-filled details in one queue and checks the original ID. For foreign nationals, the Form III particulars are laid out for the Bureau of Immigration portal, with timers for the arrival and departure filings.

    RRetoolSSupabase
  4. 04

    Route in-stay requests with response targets

    Guest messages are classified into housekeeping, maintenance, food and beverage or front desk, become tickets with response targets, and escalate to the duty manager when a target is missed. Safety, medical and security messages skip automation and alert a person at once.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformOOpenAInn8nSSlack
  5. 05

    Feedback, recovery and review replies

    At checkout guests get a short private feedback form. Low scores open a recovery case for guest relations, every guest receives the same review invitation, and AI drafts replies to new public reviews for a manager to edit and approve.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformACAnthropic ClaudeRRetool
  6. 06

    One operating view

    A daily dashboard shows pre-check-in completion, Form III filings against deadline, open and breached requests, extras taken and reviews awaiting a reply, by property and shift.

Human checkpoint

Front office staff check every original ID at arrival and submit Form III themselves on the official portal. The duty manager owns breached requests and anything involving safety. The guest relations or general manager approves every public review reply, refund and compensation offer before it is sent.

What changes

  • Shorter check-in queues, because guest details arrive before the guest does
  • Foreign guest filings tracked against the twenty-four-hour deadline instead of reconstructed from paper
  • Requests owned and visible, so issues are fixed during the stay rather than discovered in a review
  • Extras and review replies handled consistently, with recorded consent and a named approver

Start where the work repeats.

A selection from the playbook. Each blueprint shows the trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Discover and inquire · 3–5 weeks

Direct booking inquiry desk

Answer room inquiries from WhatsApp, Instagram, website chat and email with live rates and availability, offer a direct booking link, and pass group, long-stay and corporate requests to sales with the details already captured.

OTA rate consistency watch

Check every day that the prices guests see on OTAs and metasearch match what the hotel loaded, flag undercuts and stale inventory, and give the revenue manager a short exception list instead of a spreadsheet to scan.

Aggregator menu sync and rating watch

Keep Swiggy, Zomato and other ordering channels in step with what the kitchen can actually make, and give each brand and outlet a daily digest of ratings, complaints and the dishes behind them.

Group, MICE and wedding inquiry desk

How we work

A clear delivery rhythm, from discovery to daily operation.

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 01 · 1–2 weeksDiscover

    We sit with the front desk, reservations, kitchen, consultants or banquet team to map how guests actually inquire, book, arrive and complain, and which systems hold the data. We confirm what the PMS, POS, channel manager and booking systems allow through APIs or exports, and choose the first journey to automate.

  2. 02 · 1–2 weeksDesign

    We design conversation flows, guest forms, routing rules, response targets and approval points, and write the WhatsApp, SMS and email templates for approval. Consent wording, ID handling and retention are designed with the client's compliance owner before anything is built.

  3. 03 · 2–6 weeksBuild

    We build the workflows in n8n or code, the secure guest forms and staff consoles, AI prompts grounded in approved content, and the connections to the client's systems, all in a staging setup with test data.

  4. 04 · 1–2 weeksValidate & launch

    Staff test real scenarios: late arrivals, foreign guests, sold-out dishes, rebooked flights and changed guest counts. We check AI drafts against an evaluation set, launch on one property, outlet or desk first, and train every shift.

  5. 05 · Ongoing, reviewed monthlyOperate & improve

    We monitor workflow health, response targets and AI quality, fix failures, and review results with the client each month. New templates, segments, outlets and properties are added through the same approval process.

Suggested first pilot

One property or outlet, one journey, four to six weeks

We start where volume and pain are highest. For a hotel that is usually pre-arrival messages and digital pre-check-in with Form III tracking at one property, with extras and in-stay routing added after the review. For a restaurant group it is reservations or the daily close at one outlet, and for a travel company, document and payment reminders for one desk. A first-week baseline keeps the comparison honest.

  • One property, outlet or desk and one guest journey
  • Approved WhatsApp templates and a secure guest form
  • Integration with the PMS, POS or booking system in read and limited write mode
  • A staff console for the queue, with escalation to a named manager
  • Weekly check-ins and a go or no-go review at the end of the pilot

Measures

Know whether it is working.

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

First response time to inquiries

Median elapsed time from a new inquiry on any connected channel to the first meaningful reply by the system or a person, measured per channel and hour of day.

Direct booking share

Room nights, covers or trips booked through the business's own channels as a share of the total for the period, by property or outlet.

Pre-check-in completion

Arriving reservations with pre-check-in details submitted before arrival, divided by all arriving reservations that received the link.

Form III filings on time

Foreign guest arrivals and departures with Form III particulars submitted within twenty-four hours, as a share of all foreign guest arrivals and departures in the period.
